title: The Complete Egypt Travel Guide
subtitle: Five-thousand-year-old monuments, a river that built a civilisation, and Red Sea reefs among the best diving on Earth
summary: How to plan an Egypt trip: whether to focus on Cairo, a Nile cruise or the Red Sea coast, when to go to avoid the worst heat, what it costs, and a practical ten-day itinerary.

sections.title: How Egypt divides
body: Egypt genuinely divides into distinct zones along and beyond the Nile, and a first trip realistically covers the river corridor plus one coastal or desert extension.
**Cairo and the pyramids.** [[cairo-giza|Cairo and Giza]] — the capital's museums and the Pyramids of Giza, the near-universal starting point for any Egypt trip.
**The Nile corridor.** [[luxor|Luxor]], [[aswan|Aswan]] and a [[nile-cruise|Nile cruise]] between them — ancient Egypt's temple-lined heartland.
**The Red Sea coast.** [[sharm-el-sheikh|Sharm El Sheikh]], [[dahab|Dahab]] and [[hurghada|Hurghada]] — extraordinary diving and a relaxed beach counterpoint to the ruins.

**The north and the desert.** [[alexandria|Alexandria]] on the Mediterranean, and [[white-desert-bahariya|the White Desert]] and [[siwa-oasis|Siwa Oasis]] further into the Western Desert, both genuinely rewarding but off the classic first-timer route.
sections.note: Most first-time visitors genuinely combine [[cairo-giza|Cairo]] with a Nile cruise between [[luxor|Luxor]] and [[aswan|Aswan]]. The Western Desert oases are where a longer or second trip belongs.

list.title: If this is your first trip
list.text: [[cairo-giza|Cairo and Giza]], genuinely the essential starting point for any Egypt itinerary.

list.title: If you want the classic ancient Egypt route
list.text: A [[nile-cruise|Nile cruise]] between [[luxor|Luxor]] and [[aswan|Aswan]], genuinely the most efficient way to see the temple sites.

list.title: If you want world-class diving
list.text: [[dahab|Dahab]] or [[sharm-el-sheikh|Sharm El Sheikh]], both genuinely among the best diving destinations on Earth.

list.title: If you want a relaxed beach extension
list.text: [[hurghada|Hurghada]], genuinely the most resort-focused option on the Red Sea coast.

list.title: If you want somewhere genuinely different from the ruins
list.text: [[white-desert-bahariya|The White Desert]], with its otherworldly chalk formations and desert camping.

list.title: If you want real remoteness
list.text: [[siwa-oasis|Siwa Oasis]], genuinely one of Egypt's most isolated and culturally distinct destinations.

sections.title: Getting around: flights, trains, and one common mistake
body: Egypt's genuinely long north-south distances mean no single mode of transport covers the whole country — a mix of flights, trains and cruise boats is standard.
**Fly for long distances, don't drive.** [[cairo-giza|Cairo]] to [[aswan|Aswan]] genuinely takes most of a day by road versus about an hour and a half by air.
**Book a Nile cruise for Luxor to Aswan.** It's genuinely the classic, most comfortable way to see the temples along the river without repeated hotel changes.
**Don't underestimate the heat.** Sightseeing in [[luxor|Luxor]] or [[aswan|Aswan]] outside winter genuinely requires pacing around the midday sun.
**Use overnight trains for a budget-friendly link.** Sleeper cabins between [[cairo-giza|Cairo]] and [[luxor|Luxor]] or [[aswan|Aswan]] genuinely save both time and a hotel night.
**Book a private driver for the desert oases.** [[white-desert-bahariya|The White Desert]] and [[siwa-oasis|Siwa]] genuinely require experienced desert driving best left to local operators.
sections.note: Book your Nile cruise and major site tickets well ahead for peak winter travel — Egypt's most comfortable season genuinely sells out its best cruise cabins early.

sections.title: When to go
body: Egypt's desert climate genuinely means 'the best time' is mostly about avoiding extreme heat rather than chasing good weather, which is reliable and dry nearly year-round.
**Winter**, December to February, brings genuinely the mildest, most comfortable temperatures for sightseeing, also the busiest and priciest season.
**Shoulder months**, October-November and March-April, offer genuinely warm but manageable heat with thinner crowds than peak winter.
**Summer**, May to September, brings genuinely intense heat, especially in Luxor and Aswan, though the Red Sea coast stays comparatively more bearable.
**The Red Sea coast** is genuinely workable nearly year-round, making it a sensible add-on regardless of when you visit the Nile sites.
sections.note: Book Nile cruise cabins and major site tickets many months ahead for a December-February trip — this is genuinely the busiest and most tightly booked window of the year.

list.title: Four days: Cairo and Giza
list.text: [[cairo-giza|Cairo and Giza]] alone, genuinely the most popular short Egypt itinerary for a reason.
list.tip: Add the Grand Egyptian Museum to your Giza day for a genuinely complete pyramid experience.

list.title: Ten days: the classic Nile route
list.text: The itinerary on the [[c:egypt|Egypt country page]]: [[cairo-giza|Cairo]], a [[nile-cruise|Nile cruise]] through [[luxor|Luxor]] and [[aswan|Aswan]], and a Red Sea extension. A genuinely complete first look at Egypt's classic highlights.
list.tip: Book a four-night cruise rather than a shorter option — it allows a genuinely unrushed pace at each temple stop.

list.title: A week focused on the Red Sea
list.text: [[hurghada|Hurghada]], [[dahab|Dahab]] or [[sharm-el-sheikh|Sharm El Sheikh]] as a dedicated diving and relaxation trip, skipping the Nile entirely.
list.tip: Dahab genuinely offers a more laid-back, budget-friendly diving scene than Sharm El Sheikh's larger resorts.

list.title: A Western Desert add-on for a second trip
list.text: [[white-desert-bahariya|The White Desert]] and [[siwa-oasis|Siwa Oasis]], genuinely two of Egypt's most remote and rewarding corners.
list.tip: Book a genuinely reputable desert safari operator — independent desert driving here is not recommended.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Egypt?
faq.a: Ten to twelve days covers Cairo, a Nile cruise and a Red Sea extension at a reasonable pace, which is the itinerary in this guide. Four to five days is enough for Cairo and Giza alone, and genuinely still worthwhile on its own.

faq.q: Is a Nile cruise worth the cost?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's the classic, most comfortable way to see Luxor, Edfu, Kom Ombo and Aswan's temples without repeated hotel changes, and the river scenery itself is part of the experience.

faq.q: Do you need a guide at the pyramids and temples?
faq.a: Not required, but genuinely recommended — a licensed guide adds real historical context that's easy to miss exploring independently, and helps navigate persistent touting.

faq.q: When should I visit to avoid the worst heat?
faq.a: October to April offers genuinely the most comfortable temperatures, especially in Luxor and Aswan, where summer heat can exceed 40°C and become genuinely dangerous for sightseeing.
